questions.hint: GROUP BY collapses rows per region; SUM() adds up the amounts.
questions.prompt: Return each region and its total order revenue, with columns named `region` and `revenue`.
questions.solution: SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY region ORDER BY region;
questions.title: Revenue by region

questions.hint: LEFT JOIN keeps every customer; the join partner's columns are NULL when there is no match.
questions.prompt: Return the names of customers who have placed zero orders, as a single column named `name`, ordered alphabetically.
questions.solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders2 o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;
questions.title: Customers with no orders

questions.hint: SQLite's date() understands modifiers like '-30 days'. Treat 2026-09-22 as 'today'.
questions.prompt: Treat 2026-09-22 as today. Return `order_id` and `amount` for orders placed in the last 30 days (inclusive), ordered by `order_id`.
questions.solution: SELECT order_id, amount FROM orders3 WHERE order_date >= date('2026-09-22','-30 days') ORDER BY order_id;
questions.title: Orders in the last 30 days

questions.hint: Order by revenue descending and keep only the first 3 rows. There are no ties, so LIMIT is deterministic.
questions.prompt: Return the top 3 products by revenue, with columns `product` and `revenue`, ordered by revenue descending.
questions.solution: SELECT product, revenue FROM products ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3;
questions.title: Top 3 products by revenue

questions.hint: First find each customer's earliest order date, then join back to get the full order row.
questions.prompt: For each customer, return their first order: columns `name`, `order_id`, `order_date`, `amount`, ordered by customer name.
questions.solution:
SELECT c.name, o.order_id, o.order_date, o.amount
FROM customers5 c
JOIN orders5 o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN (SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_d FROM orders5 GROUP BY customer_id) f
  ON o.customer_id = f.customer_id AND o.order_date = f.first_d
ORDER BY c.name;
questions.title: Each customer's first order

questions.hint: RANK() numbers rows within each department. What should PARTITION BY be, and which direction should the salary sort go?
questions.prompt: Rank employees by salary within their department (highest salary = rank 1). Return `name`, `dept`, `salary`, `rnk`, ordered by `dept` then `rnk`.
questions.solution: SELECT name, dept, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk FROM employees ORDER BY dept, rnk;
questions.title: Rank salaries within department

questions.hint: An aggregate window function with ORDER BY in the OVER clause accumulates as the frame grows.
questions.prompt: Return each day, its revenue, and the running total of revenue so far: columns `day`, `revenue`, `running_total`, ordered by `day`.
questions.solution: SELECT day, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS running_total FROM daily ORDER BY day;
questions.title: Running total of daily revenue

questions.hint: LAG() reaches back one row. The growth formula is (this - prev) / prev; round to 4 decimals.
questions.prompt: Return each month, its revenue, and month-over-month growth vs the previous month as `mom_growth` (NULL for the first month), rounded to 4 decimals. Columns: `month`, `revenue`, `mom_growth`, ordered by `month`.
questions.title: Month-over-month growth

questions.hint: A CTE can hold per-customer totals; then compare each total to the average of all totals.
questions.prompt: Using a CTE, return customers whose total spend is strictly above the average total spend across all customers. Columns: `customer`, `total`, ordered by customer.
questions.solution:
WITH totals AS (SELECT customer, SUM(amount) AS total FROM spend GROUP BY customer)
SELECT customer, total FROM totals
WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM totals)
ORDER BY customer;
questions.title: Customers above average spend

questions.hint: ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by category gives each product a rank inside its category; filter to ranks 1 and 2.
questions.prompt: Return the top 2 products by revenue within each category. Columns: `category`, `product`, `revenue`, ordered by `category` then revenue descending.
questions.title: Top 2 products per category

questions.hint: Build one CTE of January users and one of February users, then keep the intersection.
questions.prompt: Using CTEs, return the `user_id`s of users who were active in both 2026-01 and 2026-02 (January-to-February retention), as a single column `user_id` ordered ascending.
questions.title: Two-month retention

questions.hint: AVG() as a window function with an explicit ROWS frame: 6 PRECEDING through CURRENT ROW. Round to 2 decimals.
questions.prompt: Return each day and its 7-day rolling average revenue (including the current day; fewer than 7 days at the start is fine). Columns: `day`, `rolling_avg` rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by `day`.
questions.title: 7-day rolling average

questions.hint: Join the table to itself: employees on one side, their managers on the other.
questions.prompt: Return the names of employees who earn strictly more than their direct manager, as a single column `name`, ordered alphabetically.
questions.solution: SELECT e.name FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.manager_id = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary ORDER BY e.name;
questions.title: Employees earning more than their manager

questions.hint: Find each user's first signup and first purchase, then keep users whose purchase came strictly after their signup.
questions.prompt: Return the `user_id`s of users who completed the funnel: they signed up and then made a purchase strictly after their signup. Single column `user_id`, ordered ascending.
questions.title: Funnel: signup then purchase

questions.hint: ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by user ordered by `updated` descending marks the newest row as 1; keep only those.
questions.prompt: Deduplicate: return one row per user, keeping the row with the latest `updated` timestamp. Columns: `user_id`, `val`, `updated`, ordered by `user_id`.
questions.title: Deduplicate: latest row per user
